newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-MAJOLI THINKS SHE CAN BEAT HINGIS BUT FEW OTHERS DO.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MAJOLI THINKS SHE CAN BEAT HINGIS BUT FEW OTHERS DO.

text.p: Iva Majoli promised to give Martina Hingis a hard time in the French Open women's final but her chances of inflicting on the world number one her first defeat of the year look slim.
"I beat her once," said Majoli, as if she wanted to remind everybody that Hingis could be beaten. "But in our last two matches she beat me."
Saturday's battle of teenagers between the 16-year-old Swiss and Croatia's Majoli, who is three years older, could well be a one-sided affair as Hingis looks in a class of her own.
"Okay, she's a great player but I do believe she can be beaten," Majoli said. "If I thought otherwise I'd just as well stay in bed."
Majoli, the ninth seed, struggled to move past South African Amanda Coetzer in a tense semifinal on Thursday to advance to her first-ever grand slam final.
Australian Open winner Hingis, who overcame former world number one Monica Seles after a superb fight in the other semifinal, is only one match away from her first title on the Paris clay.
But Majoli said she would do her best to upset the latest phenomenon in women's tennis.
"This is my favourite grand slam and I'm in the final," she said. "It's a great opportunity for me and I don't want to let it slip away."
Hingis, playing her first tournament since hurting her knee in a riding accident last April, has kept improving since the tournament started.

The kind of form she displayed against Seles, using a great variety of shots and showing superior intelligence to counter her opponent's raw power, suggested she might be a little too smart for Majoli.

"She's consistent and she makes few mistakes," said Majoli who, like Seles, learned her trade at Nick Bollettieri's tennis academy in Bradenton, Florida. "I'll just have to be aggressive and play my game."

It will be even more difficult for Majoli as she is suffering from a cold which prevented her from sleeping before her match against Coetzer, quarter-final conqueror of defending champion Steffi Graf.

"I woke up in the middle of the night sweating and my whole body was burning hot," she said. "During the match I was under medication, not feeling too good, but I wanted to win so badly that I didn't take too much notice. After a massage and a good night's sleep I should be all right."
Hingis looked tired too after her match, refusing to answer the last questions at her post-match press conference. She had said earlier that she was still receiving treatment on her knee.
"Yesterday (Wednesday) I underwent therapy for about an hour," she said. "But it's improving every day. I could run pretty well today (Thursday). Anyway, I had to if I wanted to win the match."
Still undefeated after all the 37 matches she has played so far this year, Hingis appeared not have been too confident when she came into the tournament.
"My goal was to reach the semifinals," she said after beating Seles. "Now I'm in the final and I do feel I have a great chance of winning the tournament."
